claims.text: Faith frames traders as participants who assume or transfer price and liquidity risk rather than as owners whose case rests on business value.
The bid-ask spread is an immediate execution cost and compensation for liquidity provision, so a visible last price is not necessarily an executable price.
The chapter describes price movement as emerging from changing willingness of heterogeneous buyers and sellers, including hedgers, scalpers and speculators.
The claim that electronic execution lowers costs and enables more frequent trading is historically plausible but requires current, instrument-specific spread, fee, impact and latency evidence.

memory_delta: A trading thesis must identify which risk is being assumed, the executable spread and the participant/time horizon it expects to outlast. Price movement alone is an observation, not yet a complete trend system.
